<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Internal prefill checkpoints (RFC #52959) for Qwen GDN models (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5) on the FlashInfer GDN prefill backend. With prefix caching on (Mamba align mode), a prompt that crosses its cacheable block boundary no longer needs two forward passes: FlashInfer's prefill emits the boundary state in the same call. Kimi-K3 does the same with FlashKDA (#52789, #53614). Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) keeps main's split prefill and block: its PLE short-conv Mamba layer cannot export checkpoints, and the scheduler takes them only when every Mamba layer can.

## Claims

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 1x GB200, 8000-token prompts, on main `716961c`: TTFT −20% at concurrency 1, −12% at 4, −10% at 16. TPOT and accuracy are unchanged.
- Only enabled when the GDN prefill backend resolves to FlashInfer, prefix caching is on, and every Mamba layer of the model can export checkpoints; nothing is reserved otherwise. Triton/FLA, CuteDSL and ROCm are unchanged.
- No flags needed: align-mode blocks are put on FlashInfer's 64-token grid automatically (Qwen3.5-35B: 1056 → 1088 tokens), and only when the checkpoints are taken. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next keeps its 800-token block and main's TTFT.

## Validation

Setup: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B BF16, GB200, CUDA graphs, MRV2, `--enable-prefix-caching` (align mode; `--mamba-cache-mode` is deprecated since #60043). The baseline is main (`716961c`) with `--block-size 64`, so both arms use the same 1088-token block this PR picks automatically.

**TTFT** (`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 8000 in / 1000 out, `--ignore-eos`, 16 prompts per unit of concurrency, seed `100 + concurrency` so no prompt repeats across levels; prefix cache hit rate 0% in both arms):

| Concurrency | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 188.0 ms | 150.8 ms | −20% |
| 4 | 398.4 ms | 349.4 ms | −12% |
| 16 | 770.6 ms | 694.0 ms | −10% |

TPOT is within ±2%. The prompt's last block boundary sits at 7616 tokens: with a scheduler log, main ran all 336 prompts as 7616 + 384 tokens, and this PR ran every one in a single step with an internal checkpoint (FlashInfer emitted one state per prefill, `every_n=7616`).

Reusing one seed across concurrency levels makes the first prompts of each level repeat the previous level's, and those requests hit the prefix cache and skip the split in both arms; a run measured that way showed no gain at 4 and 16, so it is not used here.

**GSM8K** (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions; independent runs separated by `/`):

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 5-shot | 0.7915 / 0.8150 | 0.7779 / 0.7998 / 0.7908 |
| 20-shot | 0.3192 / 0.3177 | 0.3374 / 0.3245 / 0.3275 |
| 40-shot, MTP (3 tokens) | 0.7900 / 0.8082 | 0.7763 / 0.8036 |
| 20-shot, bf16 SSM cache | 0.3510 | 0.3412 |
| 20-shot, TP=2, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | – | 0.3677 |
| After merging main `716961c`: 5 / 20 / 40-shot MTP | – | 0.7915 / 0.3753 / 0.8135 |

- 5-shot prompts fit in one block, so no checkpoint is taken. The ~2-point spread between runs of the same arm is the noise floor.
- Qwen3.5 scores ~0.3 at 20-shot with a 256-token budget on both arms. Only the A/B comparison is meaningful there.
- The 20- and 40-shot runs take and resume from checkpoints (prefix hit rate 70–82% on both arms). With MTP, EAGLE block drop needs prompts longer than 2 blocks, hence 40-shot.
- The TP=2 run under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed without a sync violation.
- MRV1 not validated: main itself OOMs at KV-cache allocation in this configuration under MRV1. The checkpoint path is shared code in the GDN layer and metadata builder.

**After the review fixes** (`f3df8ff`, main `7fad7db`, default flags, so the block is the one this PR picks):

| Metric | this PR |
|---|---|
| Attention block / KV cache memory | 1088 tokens / 99.01 GiB |
| GSM8K 20-shot | 0.3601 |
| GSM8K 40-shot, MTP (3 tokens) | 0.7854 (mean acceptance length 3.55) |
| TTFT c1 / c4 / c16 (same benchmark as above) | 157.3 / 361.0 / 722.1 ms |
| TPOT c1 / c4 / c16 | 3.32 / 4.33 / 7.15 ms |

- The server ran with `--enable-prefix-caching` only and picked the 1088-token block itself.
- The 40-shot MTP run hits the prefix cache at 82%, so its requests resume from checkpoints exported with the MTP-sized conv cache.
- TTFT is 3–5% above the `716961c` run in the table above. Main was not re-measured on `7fad7db`, so that table remains the A/B comparison.
- With `7500dd1` (blocks aligned only when every Mamba layer can checkpoint), Qwen3.5-35B keeps the 1088-token block: TTFT 147.7 / 337.7 / 671.9 ms at c1 / c4 / c16, GSM8K 20-shot 0.3093.
- With `5089abd` (the plan reuses the checkpoint rows' query lengths): GSM8K 20-shot 0.3207, 40-shot MTP 0.7885, prefix hit rate 79% / 82%, so batches mix decodes and checkpointed prefills.

**Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP (3 tokens), `--enable-prefix-caching`, same TTFT benchmark; every arm on one GB200 node, main `7fad7db`):

| | main | `0b19574` | this PR (`7500dd1`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attention block | 800 | 832 | 800 |
| TTFT mean c1 / c4 / c16 | 282.1 / 354.8 / 437.4 ms | 408.3 / 506.4 / 600.3 ms | 279.6 / 358.5 / 450.2 ms |
| TTFT median c1 / c4 / c16 | 281.6 / 323.7 / 332.5 ms | 406.0 / 459.8 / 468.3 ms | 278.7 / 334.4 / 337.8 ms |
| TPOT c1 / c4 / c16 | 2.86 / 3.85 / 8.02 ms | 2.75 / 4.41 / 9.96 ms | 2.75 / 3.95 / 7.92 ms |
| GSM8K 20-shot, chat, thinking off | 0.9629 | 0.9689 | 0.9583 |

- Qwen4Exp's PLE layer is a second Mamba layer (short conv) without checkpoints, so the scheduler still splits its prefills. `0b19574` aligned the block anyway (800 → 832), which moved an 8000-token prompt's split from 7200 + 800 to 6656 + 1344. The 1344-token tail is above the 1024-token CUDA graph capture size and ran eagerly: 120 ms per step against 45 ms for the 800-token tail in a torch profile. Blocks are now aligned only when every Mamba layer declares an alignment, and the GDN layer then reserves no checkpoint block, workspace or checkpoint kernels.
- Raw-completion GSM8K scores 0 on every arm (the model ends few-shot completions immediately), hence the chat run.

**Tests** (GB200, `f3df8ff`):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py        # 5 passed (new export test x4)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py           # 62 passed
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py        # 8 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_checkpoint_state.py        # 14 passed
pytest tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py             # 46 passed
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py \
       tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py
                                                                 # 160 passed, 35 skipped (AMD-only)
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "checkpoint_grid or block_size"   # 14 passed (7500dd1)
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py           # 4 passed
# 0b19574, new:
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py::test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async_flashinfer   # 1 passed
```

- The new test in `test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py` runs FlashInfer with checkpoints and the exporter on a decode row plus three prefills, two of which checkpoint at offsets whose gcd is below both, and compares each exported recurrent state with a prefill stopped at its offset and each conv window with the raw input (both FlashInfer routes, fp32 and bf16 SSM cache). The conv cache has MTP's spec slots after the window; the test checks they stay untouched.
- `test_blocks_land_on_the_mamba_checkpoint_grid` checks that a Mamba layer declaring a 64-token checkpoint alignment moves Qwen3.5-0.8B's block from 544 to 576, and that nothing changes without one or when another Mamba layer declares none.
- `test_mamba_prefix_cache.py` scripts the align-mode split at the prompt's last block boundary step by step. On FlashInfer machines (its CI runs on H200) this PR skips that split, so all four cases failed at `prompt_2_block_size`; the align-mode LLMs now pin `gdn_prefill_backend="triton"`, which keeps the script's premise. ROCm and XPU already resolve to Triton.
- `test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async_flashinfer` (new, MRV2 + async scheduling, H200 CI job) scripts the FlashInfer schedule instead: 2B and 2B + 10 prompts run in one step, 10B and 10B + 10 in two (5B, then the rest with the 9B checkpoint), with the checkpoint block and state copies asserted at each step. It then checks the state a 2B + 10 prefill exports at B against the final state of a prefill that stops at B, over distinct tokens: the conv window matches exactly and the SSM state within 2.7e-3 relative error.

## Details

- **Kernel.** `flashinfer.gdn_prefill.chunk_gated_delta_rule` can emit a state every N tokens of each sequence (`state_checkpoints`, `checkpoint_cu_starts`, `checkpoint_every_n_tokens`), where N is a multiple of 64. On GB200, each emitted state matches a separate run truncated at that position (max abs err 5e-3), and the final state is bit-identical with checkpoints on.
- **Plan.** Computed once per step on the host from `MambaPrefillCheckpointBuilder`'s offsets, so the scheduler and `MambaManager` agree on which rows checkpoint.
  - N is the gcd of the batch's offsets.
  - The plan also has the per-sequence checkpoint counts and each row's index into the emitted states.
  - It uses the host copies of the offsets (from #57329) and of the rows' query lengths on `MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata`, so there is no device→host sync, and the counts and rows go to the device in one copy. It runs only in steps that take a checkpoint; at 16 rows the host work is a few µs.
- **Forward.** A step with checkpoints calls `fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule` directly with the plan; every other step calls `ChunkGatedDeltaRule` as before, whose signatures are unchanged.
- **Export.** Exporting a checkpoint is the same copy for every backend: the conv window ending at the offset, and one recurrent state picked out of a buffer the prefill kernel emitted.
  - `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter` was an ABC with one implementation (Kimi-K3's, in `kda_checkpoint.py`). That implementation now is the class, in `layers/mamba/checkpoint.py`, with an optional `recurrent_rows` that picks each row's state out of the buffer; by default row `i` holds checkpoint `i`'s.
  - GDN passes FlashInfer's buffer and the plan's rows, so the only copy is one state per checkpointed row; decode rows and rows without a checkpoint are masked.
  - `FlashKDAPrefillCheckpointExporter` stays as a subclass, so the Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash code is untouched. Mamba2's `ssd_checkpoint` kernel is the same copy with `chunk_idx` as the rows; folding it in is left to #61466.
  - GDN exports `conv_kernel_size - 1` columns of the conv window. Under MTP the conv cache has `num_spec` more, which the conv kernels never read (thanks @fuscof-ibm).
  - FlashInfer computes in an FP32 state (the wrapper upcasts), so the checkpoint buffer is FP32. The store casts it to the cache dtype.
- **Block alignment.** Offsets must be multiples of 64. Qwen3.5-35B's align block is 1056 (16 × 66), so every other checkpoint would be declined and fall back to a split prefill.
  - Mamba layers declare the alignment their checkpoints need through `MambaBase.get_prefill_checkpoint_alignment()`; GDN returns 64 when it takes FlashInfer checkpoints. When every Mamba layer declares one (`get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_alignment`), `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` makes align-mode blocks a multiple of their LCM (1056 → 1088). Otherwise the scheduler never takes internal checkpoints, so the block and the GDN spec stay as on main. sglang avoids this the same way, by keeping its Mamba cache grid at max(64, page_size).
  - The spec's `prefill_checkpoint_alignment` is the prefix-cache grid: the block, or `lcm(prefix_match_unit, 64)` when a finer match unit is set. A checkpoint off it falls back to the split prefill.
- **Workspace.** With every offset on the grid, FlashInfer's stride (their gcd) is a multiple of it, so a batch emits at most one state per grid step. The buffer holds `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, grid)` FP32 states, sized at profile time once the block is final: 16 states (32 MiB) on Qwen3.5-35B TP1 with 16384 batched tokens.
- **Warmup.** FlashInfer compiles separate CuTeDSL kernels for its context-parallel and regular routes, each with and without checkpoints. The GDN warmup now calls all four (`use_cp="auto"` and `False`). Before this, it only reached the route a single 64-token sequence takes, so the others compiled during serving (seconds on a cold cache).

**Tradeoffs.**

- The 64-aligned block is ~3% larger.
- Qwen4Exp gains nothing yet: its PLE short conv would need its own checkpoint export.
- With a `prefix_match_unit` finer than the block, the grid shrinks to `lcm(prefix_match_unit, 64)`, and the workspace and the states FlashInfer writes grow with it. In the worst case (a 64-token grid) this is 0.5 GiB and about 1 ms per 8k-token step.
- Validated on SM100 (GB200) only. FlashInfer also supports these checkpoints on SM90 and SM120.
- The shared Triton store kernel still compiles on first use, because its strides depend on the allocated KV cache.

**Related / not a duplicate.** No open PR adds internal checkpoints for GDN (searched 2026-10-05).

- #57329 (merged) does this for Mamba2; this PR reuses its host `offsets` on `MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata`.
- #61466 (draft) follows up: every Mamba layer declares its alignment through the same method, and the base spec derives the checkpoint fields from it.
- #50372 (open) edits FlashInfer GDN prefill state I/O in the same file; the overlap is mechanical only.
- #55873/#55875/#55876 add application-directed checkpoints via scheduler splits.

🔴 Align-mode serving on SM12.x GPUs may crash on the first checkpointed prefill; on the base branch these GPUs safely use the split-prefill fallback. Fix: enable checkpoints only on SM90 and SM10.x. Use the capability check the test uses, so every other FlashInfer arch keeps the split-prefill path and the spec's `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks` stays 0 there.

<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

🔴 With dual-batch overlap on, a checkpointed prefill in the second microbatch can raise "Workspace is locked" and crash the engine. The ~256 MiB checkpoint buffer is reserved only inside `_warmup_prefill_kernels`, which runs once per layer behind `_prefill_kernels_warmed_up`. Workspaces are per ubatch/lane (`_get_workspace_id`), so only the ubatch that ran warmup first gets sized. Fix: reserve `_checkpoint_buffer_spec` in every ubatch/lane workspace before `lock_workspace()`. For example, do the reservation outside the once-per-layer flag on every profiling call, or iterate the ubatch IDs.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Condition: `--enable-dbo` (or ubatch_size > 1) together with align mode and the FlashInfer GDN backend. `profile_run` calls `_dummy_run` with `allow_microbatching=True` (gpu_model_runner.py:6133+), so the dummy batch runs as two ubatches. Each layer's first `_warmup_prefill_kernels` call sets `_prefill_kernels_warmed_up` and calls `get_simultaneous(self._checkpoint_buffer_spec)` only in the current ubatch's workspace. The other ubatch returns early and is never sized. After `lock_workspace()`, `_forward_core` calls `current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous(self._checkpoint_buffer_spec)` (line ~1755) from ubatch 1 for a checkpointed prefill. `_ensure_workspace_size` (workspace.py:209-245) then raises AssertionError "Workspace is locked but allocation ... requires" unless another consumer already grew that ubatch's slot past cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, grid) FP32 states (256 MiB on Qwen3.5-35B). The base branch has no such allocation, so DBO serving works there.

**Verification:** The checkpoint buffer is reserved only at qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:1252-1254, inside `_warmup_prefill_kernels`, behind a per-layer flag. After `lock_workspace()` (gpu_model_runner.py:6575), `get_simultaneous(self._checkpoint_buffer_spec)` runs under microbatch 1; if that slot is smaller, the assertion fires and the step crashes. On the base branch this path does not exist.

</details>

🔴 With MTP/EAGLE on, a request resuming from a FlashInfer GDN checkpoint gets a conv state shifted by `num_spec` tokens, so its outputs silently drift. The exporter is built with the default `state_len`, so it copies `conv_state.shape[-1]` = `conv_kernel_size - 1 + num_spec` tokens. The conv kernels read only the first `conv_kernel_size - 1` slots, newest last. Fix: build it as `FlashInferGDNPrefillCheckpointExporter(state_len=self.conv_kernel_size - 1)`, as GLM5next's KDA layer does (`state_len=self.conv_size - 1`). That writes the checkpoint in the same layout `causal_conv1d_fn` uses.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: `--mamba-cache-mode align`, FlashInfer GDN prefill and `num_speculative_tokens = k > 0` (MTP). With spec decode on, `get_state_shape` (qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:495) passes `num_spec` to `gated_delta_net_state_shape`, which sizes the conv state as `conv_kernel_size - 1 + num_spec` (mamba_utils.py:294). `FlashInferGDNPrefillCheckpointExporter()` (line 645) leaves `state_len=None`, so `export` uses `conv_state.shape[-1]` = 3+k (kda_checkpoint.py:42). But `causal_conv1d_fn` uses `state_len = KERNEL_WIDTH - 1` and reads the initial state from slots 0..2, newest at slot 2 (causal_conv1d.py:61,123). A request that hits this checkpoint therefore resumes with tokens end-3-k..end-1-k instead of end-3..end-1 in every GDN layer, and its outputs are silently wrong. On the base branch the scheduler splits the prefill at that boundary, so `causal_conv1d_fn` writes the checkpoint block in the correct layout. The new test uses `state_len=3` with no spec slots, so it does not catch this.

**Verification:** Trigger: align mode with the FlashInfer GDN prefill backend and MTP (num_speculative_tokens = k > 0). `gated_delta_net_state_shape` sizes the conv state as `conv_kernel_size - 1 + num_spec` (mamba_utils.py:292-295). The exporter is built as `FlashInferGDNPrefillCheckpointExporter()` (line 645), so `export` uses `state_len = conv_state.shape[-1]` (kda_checkpoint.py:42-44), but `causal_conv1d_fn` reads K-1 slots (causal_conv1d.py:61-63).

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Internal prefill checkpoints (RFC #52959) for Qwen GDN models (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5) on the FlashInfer GDN prefill backend. With prefix caching on (Mamba align mode), a prompt that crosses its cacheable block boundary no longer needs two forward passes: FlashInfer's prefill emits the boundary state in the same call. Kimi-K3 does the same with FlashKDA (#52789, #53614). Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) keeps main's split prefill and block: its PLE short-conv Mamba layer cannot export checkpoints, and the scheduler takes them only when every Mamba layer can.

## Claims

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 1x GB200, 8000-token prompts, on main `716961c`: TTFT −20% at concurrency 1, −12% at 4, −10% at 16. TPOT and accuracy are unchanged.
- Only enabled when the GDN prefill backend resolves to FlashInfer, prefix caching is on, and every Mamba layer of the model can export checkpoints; nothing is reserved otherwise. Triton/FLA, CuteDSL and ROCm are unchanged.
- No flags needed: align-mode blocks are put on FlashInfer's 64-token grid automatically (Qwen3.5-35B: 1056 → 1088 tokens), and only when the checkpoints are taken. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next keeps its 800-token block and main's TTFT.

## Validation

Setup: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B BF16, GB200, CUDA graphs, MRV2, `--enable-prefix-caching` (align mode; `--mamba-cache-mode` is deprecated since #60043). The baseline is main (`716961c`) with `--block-size 64`, so both arms use the same 1088-token block this PR picks automatically.

**TTFT** (`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 8000 in / 1000 out, `--ignore-eos`, 16 prompts per unit of concurrency, seed `100 + concurrency` so no prompt repeats across levels; prefix cache hit rate 0% in both arms):

| Concurrency | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 188.0 ms | 150.8 ms | −20% |
| 4 | 398.4 ms | 349.4 ms | −12% |
| 16 | 770.6 ms | 694.0 ms | −10% |

TPOT is within ±2%. The prompt's last block boundary sits at 7616 tokens: with a scheduler log, main ran all 336 prompts as 7616 + 384 tokens, and this PR ran every one in a single step with an internal checkpoint (FlashInfer emitted one state per prefill, `every_n=7616`).

Reusing one seed across concurrency levels makes the first prompts of each level repeat the previous level's, and those requests hit the prefix cache and skip the split in both arms; a run measured that way showed no gain at 4 and 16, so it is not used here.

**GSM8K** (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions; independent runs separated by `/`):

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 5-shot | 0.7915 / 0.8150 | 0.7779 / 0.7998 / 0.7908 |
| 20-shot | 0.3192 / 0.3177 | 0.3374 / 0.3245 / 0.3275 |
| 40-shot, MTP (3 tokens) | 0.7900 / 0.8082 | 0.7763 / 0.8036 |
| 20-shot, bf16 SSM cache | 0.3510 | 0.3412 |
| 20-shot, TP=2, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | – | 0.3677 |
| After merging main `716961c`: 5 / 20 / 40-shot MTP | – | 0.7915 / 0.3753 / 0.8135 |

- 5-shot prompts fit in one block, so no checkpoint is taken. The ~2-point spread between runs of the same arm is the noise floor.
- Qwen3.5 scores ~0.3 at 20-shot with a 256-token budget on both arms. Only the A/B comparison is meaningful there.
- The 20- and 40-shot runs take and resume from checkpoints (prefix hit rate 70–82% on both arms). With MTP, EAGLE block drop needs prompts longer than 2 blocks, hence 40-shot.
- The TP=2 run under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed without a sync violation.
- MRV1 not validated: main itself OOMs at KV-cache allocation in this configuration under MRV1. The checkpoint path is shared code in the GDN layer and metadata builder.

**After the review fixes** (`f3df8ff`, main `7fad7db`, default flags, so the block is the one this PR picks):

| Metric | this PR |
|---|---|
| Attention block / KV cache memory | 1088 tokens / 99.01 GiB |
| GSM8K 20-shot | 0.3601 |
| GSM8K 40-shot, MTP (3 tokens) | 0.7854 (mean acceptance length 3.55) |
| TTFT c1 / c4 / c16 (same benchmark as above) | 157.3 / 361.0 / 722.1 ms |
| TPOT c1 / c4 / c16 | 3.32 / 4.33 / 7.15 ms |

- The server ran with `--enable-prefix-caching` only and picked the 1088-token block itself.
- The 40-shot MTP run hits the prefix cache at 82%, so its requests resume from checkpoints exported with the MTP-sized conv cache.
- TTFT is 3–5% above the `716961c` run in the table above. Main was not re-measured on `7fad7db`, so that table remains the A/B comparison.
- With `7500dd1` (blocks aligned only when every Mamba layer can checkpoint), Qwen3.5-35B keeps the 1088-token block: TTFT 147.7 / 337.7 / 671.9 ms at c1 / c4 / c16, GSM8K 20-shot 0.3093.
- With `5089abd` (the plan reuses the checkpoint rows' query lengths): GSM8K 20-shot 0.3207, 40-shot MTP 0.7885, prefix hit rate 79% / 82%, so batches mix decodes and checkpointed prefills.

**Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP (3 tokens), `--enable-prefix-caching`, same TTFT benchmark; every arm on one GB200 node, main `7fad7db`):

| | main | `0b19574` | this PR (`7500dd1`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attention block | 800 | 832 | 800 |
| TTFT mean c1 / c4 / c16 | 282.1 / 354.8 / 437.4 ms | 408.3 / 506.4 / 600.3 ms | 279.6 / 358.5 / 450.2 ms |
| TTFT median c1 / c4 / c16 | 281.6 / 323.7 / 332.5 ms | 406.0 / 459.8 / 468.3 ms | 278.7 / 334.4 / 337.8 ms |
| TPOT c1 / c4 / c16 | 2.86 / 3.85 / 8.02 ms | 2.75 / 4.41 / 9.96 ms | 2.75 / 3.95 / 7.92 ms |
| GSM8K 20-shot, chat, thinking off | 0.9629 | 0.9689 | 0.9583 |

- Qwen4Exp's PLE layer is a second Mamba layer (short conv) without checkpoints, so the scheduler still splits its prefills. `0b19574` aligned the block anyway (800 → 832), which moved an 8000-token prompt's split from 7200 + 800 to 6656 + 1344. The 1344-token tail is above the 1024-token CUDA graph capture size and ran eagerly: 120 ms per step against 45 ms for the 800-token tail in a torch profile. Blocks are now aligned only when every Mamba layer declares an alignment, and the GDN layer then reserves no checkpoint block, workspace or checkpoint kernels.
- Raw-completion GSM8K scores 0 on every arm (the model ends few-shot completions immediately), hence the chat run.

**Tests** (GB200, `f3df8ff`):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py        # 5 passed (new export test x4)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py           # 62 passed
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py        # 8 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_checkpoint_state.py        # 14 passed
pytest tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py             # 46 passed
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py \
       tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py
                                                                 # 160 passed, 35 skipped (AMD-only)
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "checkpoint_grid or block_size"   # 14 passed (7500dd1)
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py           # 4 passed
# 0b19574, new:
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py::test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async_flashinfer   # 1 passed
```

- The new test in `test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py` runs FlashInfer with checkpoints and the exporter on a decode row plus three prefills, two of which checkpoint at offsets whose gcd is below both, and compares each exported recurrent state with a prefill stopped at its offset and each conv window with the raw input (both FlashInfer routes, fp32 and bf16 SSM cache). The conv cache has MTP's spec slots after the window; the test checks they stay untouched.
- `test_blocks_land_on_the_mamba_checkpoint_grid` checks that a Mamba layer declaring a 64-token checkpoint alignment moves Qwen3.5-0.8B's block from 544 to 576, and that nothing changes without one or when another Mamba layer declares none.
- `test_mamba_prefix_cache.py` scripts the align-mode split at the prompt's last block boundary step by step. On FlashInfer machines (its CI runs on H200) this PR skips that split, so all four cases failed at `prompt_2_block_size`; the align-mode LLMs now pin `gdn_prefill_backend="triton"`, which keeps the script's premise. ROCm and XPU already resolve to Triton.
- `test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async_flashinfer` (new, MRV2 + async scheduling, H200 CI job) scripts the FlashInfer schedule instead: 2B and 2B + 10 prompts run in one step, 10B and 10B + 10 in two (5B, then the rest with the 9B checkpoint), with the checkpoint block and state copies asserted at each step. It then checks the state a 2B + 10 prefill exports at B against the final state of a prefill that stops at B, over distinct tokens: the conv window matches exactly and the SSM state within 2.7e-3 relative error.

## Details

- **Kernel.** `flashinfer.gdn_prefill.chunk_gated_delta_rule` can emit a state every N tokens of each sequence (`state_checkpoints`, `checkpoint_cu_starts`, `checkpoint_every_n_tokens`), where N is a multiple of 64. On GB200, each emitted state matches a separate run truncated at that position (max abs err 5e-3), and the final state is bit-identical with checkpoints on.
- **Plan.** Computed once per step on the host from `MambaPrefillCheckpointBuilder`'s offsets, so the scheduler and `MambaManager` agree on which rows checkpoint.
  - N is the gcd of the batch's offsets.
  - The plan also has the per-sequence checkpoint counts and each row's index into the emitted states.
  - It uses the host copies of the offsets (from #57329) and of the rows' query lengths on `MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata`, so there is no device→host sync, and the counts and rows go to the device in one copy. It runs only in steps that take a checkpoint; at 16 rows the host work is a few µs.
- **Forward.** A step with checkpoints calls `fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule` directly with the plan; every other step calls `ChunkGatedDeltaRule` as before, whose signatures are unchanged.
- **Export.** Exporting a checkpoint is the same copy for every backend: the conv window ending at the offset, and one recurrent state picked out of a buffer the prefill kernel emitted.
  - `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter` was an ABC with one implementation (Kimi-K3's, in `kda_checkpoint.py`). That implementation now is the class, in `layers/mamba/checkpoint.py`, with an optional `recurrent_rows` that picks each row's state out of the buffer; by default row `i` holds checkpoint `i`'s.
  - GDN passes FlashInfer's buffer and the plan's rows, so the only copy is one state per checkpointed row; decode rows and rows without a checkpoint are masked.
  - `FlashKDAPrefillCheckpointExporter` stays as a subclass, so the Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash code is untouched. Mamba2's `ssd_checkpoint` kernel is the same copy with `chunk_idx` as the rows; folding it in is left to #61466.
  - GDN exports `conv_kernel_size - 1` columns of the conv window. Under MTP the conv cache has `num_spec` more, which the conv kernels never read (thanks @fuscof-ibm).
  - FlashInfer computes in an FP32 state (the wrapper upcasts), so the checkpoint buffer is FP32. The store casts it to the cache dtype.
- **Block alignment.** Offsets must be multiples of 64. Qwen3.5-35B's align block is 1056 (16 × 66), so every other checkpoint would be declined and fall back to a split prefill.
  - Mamba layers declare the alignment their checkpoints need through `MambaBase.get_prefill_checkpoint_alignment()`; GDN returns 64 when it takes FlashInfer checkpoints. When every Mamba layer declares one (`get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_alignment`), `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` makes align-mode blocks a multiple of their LCM (1056 → 1088). Otherwise the scheduler never takes internal checkpoints, so the block and the GDN spec stay as on main. sglang avoids this the same way, by keeping its Mamba cache grid at max(64, page_size).
  - The spec's `prefill_checkpoint_alignment` is the prefix-cache grid: the block, or `lcm(prefix_match_unit, 64)` when a finer match unit is set. A checkpoint off it falls back to the split prefill.
- **Workspace.** With every offset on the grid, FlashInfer's stride (their gcd) is a multiple of it, so a batch emits at most one state per grid step. The buffer holds `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, grid)` FP32 states, sized at profile time once the block is final: 16 states (32 MiB) on Qwen3.5-35B TP1 with 16384 batched tokens.
- **Warmup.** FlashInfer compiles separate CuTeDSL kernels for its context-parallel and regular routes, each with and without checkpoints. The GDN warmup now calls all four (`use_cp="auto"` and `False`). Before this, it only reached the route a single 64-token sequence takes, so the others compiled during serving (seconds on a cold cache).

**Tradeoffs.**

- The 64-aligned block is ~3% larger.
- Qwen4Exp gains nothing yet: its PLE short conv would need its own checkpoint export.
- With a `prefix_match_unit` finer than the block, the grid shrinks to `lcm(prefix_match_unit, 64)`, and the workspace and the states FlashInfer writes grow with it. In the worst case (a 64-token grid) this is 0.5 GiB and about 1 ms per 8k-token step.
- Validated on SM100 (GB200) only. FlashInfer also supports these checkpoints on SM90 and SM120.
- The shared Triton store kernel still compiles on first use, because its strides depend on the allocated KV cache.

**Related / not a duplicate.** No open PR adds internal checkpoints for GDN (searched 2026-10-05).

- #57329 (merged) does this for Mamba2; this PR reuses its host `offsets` on `MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata`.
- #61466 (draft) follows up: every Mamba layer declares its alignment through the same method, and the base spec derives the checkpoint fields from it.
- #50372 (open) edits FlashInfer GDN prefill state I/O in the same file; the overlap is mechanical only.
- #55873/#55875/#55876 add application-directed checkpoints via scheduler splits.

🔴 With MTP/EAGLE on, a request resuming from a FlashInfer GDN checkpoint gets a conv state shifted by `num_spec` tokens, so its outputs silently drift. The exporter is built with the default `state_len`, so it copies `conv_state.shape[-1]` = `conv_kernel_size - 1 + num_spec` tokens. The conv kernels read only the first `conv_kernel_size - 1` slots, newest last. Fix: build it as `FlashInferGDNPrefillCheckpointExporter(state_len=self.conv_kernel_size - 1)`, as GLM5next's KDA layer does (`state_len=self.conv_size - 1`). That writes the checkpoint in the same layout `causal_conv1d_fn` uses.
